search_log: Searched "Sleeping Beauties Stephen King Owen King official excerpt chapter" and opened the official Stephen King/Scribner-authorized excerpt.
Searched "Sleeping Beauties Stephen Owen King point of view third person narrator" and opened the BookRags point-of-view analysis.
Searched "Sleeping Beauties novel excerpt Evie Clint Lila official publisher" and inspected the 40-page Penguin Random House German-edition excerpt.
Searched "Sleeping Beauties multiple narrators third person review"; results mentioned multiple viewpoints but did not establish alternating grammatical persons.

Searched the exact first-person quote "That instinct, to doubt what women say"; a review attributed the reflection to Lila, confirming it is character-level material rather than a participating base narrator.

Searched the exact line "I can't stand to hope unless there's a reason to"; no source with adequate surrounding context was found, so it was treated conservatively as isolated local character material in light of the independently established third-person structure.
The Simon & Schuster publisher page supplied synopsis and bibliographic confirmation but no explicit whole-book person description, so its synopsis grammar was not used as person evidence.
person_note: The controlling narration is third person, moving externally among a large cast and rendering multiple characters' thoughts. Numerous Goodreads passages independently show that pattern, especially those centered on Frank, Tiffany, Maura, Lila, Jeanette, and Evie. The authorized excerpts corroborate sustained third-person narration, while the whole-book point-of-view source explicitly calls it third-person omniscient. Generic you passages are aphorisms or free-indirect generalizations, not second-person narration. The visible I/we material in q01743 and q01749 is local character reflection, speech, or thought; the official excerpt demonstrates the same technique by embedding first-person self-address inside an otherwise third-person Lila scene. No evidence indicates sustained first-person or second-person base sections.
